arxiv-1802-06694.title: Atiyah-Hirzebruch Spectral Sequence in Band Topology: General Formalism and Topological Invariants for 230 Space Groups
arxiv-1802-06694.creator: Ken Shiozaki, Masatoshi Sato, Kiyonori Gomi
arxiv-1802-06694.description: Abstract We study the Atiyah-Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) for equivariant K K -theory in the context of band theory. Various concepts in band theory, such as irreps at high-symmetry points, compatibility relations, topological gapless points and singularities, fit naturally into the AHSS.

arxiv-2102-12383.title: 𝒄 𝟐 \boldsymbol{c_{2}} Invariants of Hourglass Chains via Quadratic Denominator Reduction This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Algebraic Structures in Perturbative Quantum Field Theory in honor of Dirk Kreimer for his 60th birthday. The full collection is available at https://www.emi
arxiv-2102-12383.creator: Oliver SCHNETZ a and Karen YEATS b
arxiv-2102-12383.description: Abstract We introduce families of four-regular graphs consisting of chains of hourglasses which are attached to a finite kernel. We prove a formula for the c 2 c_{2} invariant of these hourglass chains which only depends on the kernel. For different kernels these hourglass chains typically give rise to different c 2 c_{2} invariants.

arxiv-2104-00045.title: Eventually, geometric ( n k ) (n_{k}) configurations exist for all n n
arxiv-2104-00045.creator: Leah Wrenn Berman, Gábor Gévay, Tomaž Pisanski
arxiv-2104-00045.description: Abstract . In a series of papers and in his 2009 book on configurations Branko Grünbaum described a sequence of operations to produce new ( n 4 ) (n_{4}) configurations from various input configurations. These operations were later called the “Grünbaum Incidence Calculus”. We generalize two of these operations to produce operations on arbitrary ( n k ) (n_{k}) configurations.

arxiv-2110-04312.title: ALP Dark Matter in a Primordial Black Hole Dominated Universe
arxiv-2110-04312.creator: and Óscar Zapata
arxiv-2110-04312.description: Abstract We investigate the phenomenological consequences of axion-like particle (ALP) dark matter with an early matter domination triggered by primordial black holes (PBHs). We focus on light BHs with masses smaller than ∼ 10 9 \sim 10^{9}~ g which fully evaporate before Big Bang nucleosynthesis.

arxiv-2203-02128.title: Distributionally Robust Bayesian Optimization with φ \varphi -divergences
arxiv-2203-02128.creator: Hisham Husain, Vu Nguyen, Anton van den Hengel
arxiv-2203-02128.description: Abstract The study of robustness has received much attention due to its inevitability in data-driven settings where many systems face uncertainty. One such example of concern is Bayesian Optimization (BO), where uncertainty is multi-faceted, yet there only exists a limited number of works dedicated to this direction. In particular, there is the work of Kirschner et al.

arxiv-2208-12272.title: Operator Growth in Open Quantum Systems
arxiv-2208-12272.creator: Thomas Schuster, Norman Y. Yao
arxiv-2208-12272.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Thomas Schuster, Norman Y. Yao. The spreading of quantum information in closed systems, often termed scrambling, is a hallmark of many-body quantum dynamics. In open systems, scrambling competes with noise, errors and decoherence. Here, we provide a universal framework that describes the scrambling of quantum information in open systems: we predict that the effect of open-system dynamics is fundamentally controlled by operator size distributions and independent of the microscopic error mechanism.

arxiv-2211-06446.title: K → μ + ​ μ − K\to\mu^{+}\mu^{-} as a third kaon golden mode
arxiv-2211-06446.creator: Avital Dery
arxiv-2211-06446.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Avital Dery. Recent progress has demonstrated that the K → μ + ​ μ − K\to\mu^{+}\mu^{-} decay carries clean short-distance information, attainable from a measurement of time-dependence sensitive to K L − K S K_{L}-K_{S} interference effects. We review the ingredients that go into this proposed extraction, and discuss the sensitivity to the CKM parameter η ¯ \bar{\eta} as well as to various NP scenarios.

arxiv-2306-14152.title: Low-Rank Prune-And-Factorize for Language Model Compression
arxiv-2306-14152.creator: Siyu Ren Kenny Q. ZhuShanghai Jiao Tong UniversityShanghai, Chinaroy0702@sjtu.edu.cn, kzhu@cs.sjtu.edu.cn
arxiv-2306-14152.description: Abstract The components underpinning PLMs—large weight matrices—were shown to bear considerable redundancy. Matrix factorization, a well-established technique from matrix theory, has been utilized to reduce the number of parameters in PLM. However, it fails to retain satisfactory performance under moderate to high compression rate.

arxiv-2308-07705.title: Parametric entropy based Cluster Centriod Initialization for k k -means clustering of various Image datasets PubID: pubid:
arxiv-2308-07705.creator: Faheem Hussayn 1 , Shahid M Shah 2
arxiv-2308-07705.description: Abstract One of the most employed yet simple algorithm for cluster analysis is the k k -means algorithm. k k -means has successfully witnessed its use in artificial intelligence, market segmentation, fraud detection, data mining, psychology, etc., only to name a few. The k k -means algorithm, however, does not always yield the best quality results.

arxiv-2401-11133.title: Field redefinition invariant Lagrange multiplier formalism with gauge symmetries
arxiv-2401-11133.creator: D. G. C. McKeon, F. T. Brandt, S. Martins-Filho
arxiv-2401-11133.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by D. G. C. McKeon, F. T. Brandt, S. Martins-Filho. It has been shown that by using a Lagrange multiplier field to ensure that the classical equations of motion are satisfied, radiative effects beyond one-loop order are eliminated. It has also been shown that through the contribution of some additional ghost fields, the effective action becomes form invariant under a redefinition of field variables, and furthermore, the usual one-loop results coincide with the quantum corrections obtained from this effective action.

arxiv-2502-05646.title: Helix curves of the unit tangent bundle of a pseudo-Riemannian surface
arxiv-2502-05646.creator: Mohamed Tahar Kadaoui ABBASSI, Khadija BOULAGOUAZ
arxiv-2502-05646.description: Abstract Abstract . In this paper, we classify helix (spacelike, timelike and null) curves, directed by the geodesic flow vector field, on the (3-dimensional) unit tangent bundle of a pseudo-Riemannian surface of constant Gaussian curvature endowed with a pseudo-Riemannian g -natural metric of Kaluza-Klein type.

arxiv-2601-15760.title: Improving the efficiency of QAOA using efficient parameter transfer initialization and targeted-single-layer regularized optimization with minimal performance degradation
arxiv-2601-15760.creator: Shubham Patel, Utkarsh Mishra
arxiv-2601-15760.description: Abstract Quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) have promising applications in combinatorial optimization problems (COPs). We investigated the MaxCut problem in three different families of graphs using QAOA ansats with parameter transfer initialization followed by targeted-single-layer optimization. For 3 3 -regular (3R), Erdős–Rényi (ER), and Barabási–Albert (BA) graphs, the parameter transfer approach achieved mean approximation ratios of 0.9443 0.

pmc-10485238.title: Elusive long‐standing intraoral foreign body: A rare encounter
pmc-10485238.creator: Chandini R, Saranya R, Murali Balasubramaniam, Ranjini Rajkumar, Safal Dhungel, Snehashish Ghosh
pmc-10485238.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Key Clinical MessageForeign body ingestion/aspiration can occur during orthodontic procedures that may be of minimal risk or lead to acute medical and life‐threatening emergencies. The present report describes a rare case of retained orthodontic wire fragment in the masticator space for nearly two decades identified as an incidental radiographic finding, highlighting the importance of optimum care in the dental clinic at all times be it surgical or nonsurgical intervention.

pmc-11539392.title: Impacts of Climate Warming on the Body Composition of Patients Undergoing Maintenance Hemodialysis
pmc-11539392.creator: Wen-Fang Chiang, Po-Jen Hsiao, Kun-Lin Wu, Ruei-Lin Wang, Chi-Ming Chu, Jenq-Shyong Chan
pmc-11539392.description: Background: Climate change, with increasing temperatures, poses a health threat to patients on maintenance hemodialysis (MHD). Seasonal variations in body composition have been documented in this population. We hypothesized that climate warming could further exacerbate these effects. In this study we investigated the impact of climate warming on the body composition of MHD patients residing in subtropical Taiwan.

pmc-11621859.title: The Diagnosis and Prognosis Value of Circulating Exosomal lncRNA MALAT1 and LNC_000226 in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction: An Observational Study
pmc-11621859.creator: Xiaodong Gu, Jingyuan Hou, Ruiqiang Weng, Jiawei Rao, Sudong Liu
pmc-11621859.description: BackgroundAcute myocardial infarction (AMI) stands as a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. This study aims to explore the potential roles of circulating exosomal lncRNA MALAT1 and LNC_000226 in AMI diagnosis and prognosis.MethodsThis retrospective observational study included 90 patients with AMI and 88 patients with normal coronary artery (NCA).

pmc-12563169.title: CCNA2 and CCNB3 as Early Potential Molecular Candidates of Oocyte Maturation in Cumulus-Oophorous Complex Cells from Follicular Fluid
pmc-12563169.creator: Nergis Özlem Kılıç, Çağrı Öner, Duygu Kütük, Belgin Selam, İbrahim Orçun Olcay, Ertuğrul Çolak, Edvīns Miklaševičs
pmc-12563169.description: Background/Objectives: Oocyte maturation is a process involving both nuclear and cytoplasmic development regulated by epigenetic changes in gene expression. Cyclin-B3 (CCNB3) and cyclin-A2 (CCNA2) genes are thought to be involved in oocyte maturation; however, the expression profiles and key function in Metaphase-I (MI) and Metaphase-II (MII) phases have yet to be fully elucidated.

pmc-12567547.title: Breakfast Skipping Among Dormitory- and Home-Residing High School Students: Insights from the Korea Youth Risk Behavior Survey 2018–2024
pmc-12567547.creator: Jeong Mi Lee, Jee-Seon Shim, Pilar Aranda Ramírez
pmc-12567547.description: Background/Objectives: Skipping breakfast is common among adolescents. Providing breakfast at school is a potential solution; however, its effectiveness remains unclear. This study aimed to compare breakfast skipping between dormitory- and home-residing high school students, analyze trends over time, and identify reasons for skipping breakfast.

pmc-12631116.title: ETV4 interacts with LOXL2 to induce epigenetic activation of NID1 during colorectal cancer progression
pmc-12631116.creator: Tinghui Jiang, Xin Liu, Hao Liu, Kailong Du, Yitao Wang, Hui Fan, Ying Zhang, Lin Cui, Hewei Zhang, Chundong Zhang, Yong Zhu, Zhongyu Liu, Youquan Bu, Yunlong Lei
pmc-12631116.description: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most common malignant cancers worldwide and its poor prognosis is mainly caused by metastasis. Although extensive studies, the potential molecular mechanisms of CRC metastasis are not fully understood. In the present study, we found that ETV4 was remarkably upregulated in CRC and its overexpression correlated with lymph node metastasis.

pmc-12636382.title: Human and zebrafish mineralocorticoid receptors reporter cell assays to assess the activity of chemicals
pmc-12636382.creator: Anna Toso, Abdelhay Boulahtouf, Marina Grimaldi, Audrey Sansaloni, Yoshinao Katsu, Michael E Baker, Aurélie Escande, Clémentine Garoche, Selim Aït-Aïssa, Patrick Balaguer
pmc-12636382.description: SummaryThe action of environmental chemicals (ECs) on the mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) has been suggested to impair physiological processes regulated by this nuclear receptor. However, it remains understudied both as a target of ECs and with respect to potential species-specific differences.

pmc-12715197.title: A Meta-Analysis of Social and Contextual Correlates of Migrant Adaptation to Living in Receiving Societies
pmc-12715197.creator: Kinga Bierwiaczonek, Dinh H Vu, Rongtian Tong, Mike W-L Cheung, Nora C G Benningstad, Evita van Duin, Karine Lindholm, Colleen Ward, Jonas R Kunst
pmc-12715197.description: International migration has been consistently rising in modern times, and understanding what factors are associated with the successful inclusion of migrants is urgent. This meta-analysis helps pinpoint such factors by identifying the most robust social and contextual correlates of successful migrant adaptation to living in the receiving societies.

pmc-13094424.title: ONMORE-Africa: diagnosing and building real-world oncology studies in Morocco and Africa
pmc-13094424.creator: HA Tafenzi, F Selmouni, H Elmarrachi, N Ismaili, I Essadi, R Belbaraka
pmc-13094424.description: Highlights•ONMORE-Africa: first standardised assessment of Moroccan oncology infrastructure.•Quantifies work force shortages, consumables, biobanking, and digital gaps.•Defines lean minimum dataset and interoperability standards for pooled RWE.•Staged implementation, pilot testing, quality assurance, and capacity building for regional RWE.•Enables co-design of policy, training, and registry pilots with stakeholders.

pmc-13463967.title: Combined autogenous fascia lata graft bridging with biceps transposition versus partial repair for massive rotator cuff tears: a retrospective comparative study
pmc-13463967.creator: Shaohua Zhang, Qingsong Zhang, Yushun Fang, Ming Tang, Yanan Li, Jun Xiong, Zhujun Wang, Tao Li
pmc-13463967.description: BackgroundGraft bridging (GB) and long head of the biceps tendon (LHBT)—based reconstructive techniques have been used to manage massive rotator cuff tears (MRCTs); however, their clinical outcomes remain variable. In this study, we explored a combined strategy of autogenous fascia lata graft bridging with LHBT transposition.

pmc-13511600.title: Working Memory Impairment Induced by Chemotherapy—A Narrative Review
pmc-13511600.creator: Nikola M. Stojanović, Mihajlo Marjanović, Milan N. Petković, Ivana Kostić Petrović, Milica Radić
pmc-13511600.description: Highlights What are the main findings? This review integrates current evidence linking chemotherapy-induced molecular alterations with the neuroanatomical substrates of working memory.Different chemotherapeutic agents converge on common mechanisms, including oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and blood–brain barrier disruption, ultimately affecting neural networks responsible for working memory. What are the implications of the main findings?

uslaw-usc-t18-s877.title: 18 U.S.C. § 877 — Mailing threatening communications from foreign country
uslaw-usc-t18-s877.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s877.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part I (Crimes); Chapter 41 (Extortion And Threats). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Whoever knowingly deposits in any post office or authorized depository for mail matter of any foreign country any communication addressed to any person within the United States, for the purpose of having such communication delivered by the post office establishment.
